K.V.N. Rajesh, Ph.D. 6mo Report this post “More than 70% of students in India don’t know what to study after Class 10 or 12,” Pause for a moment and think about that number. Seventy percent is not just confusion at an individual level; it reflects a much deeper gap in the system. Students are expected to make one of the most important decisions of their lives at the age of 15 or 16, yet very few are actually equipped to make that choice. We grow up hearing the same advice study hard, score well, and choose the right stream. But no one really explains how to choose. Science, Commerce, or Arts often becomes less about interest and more about marks, peer influence, or what is considered “safe.” Rarely is the decision based on genuine curiosity, strengths, or awareness of real-world opportunities. And this is where the long-term impact begins. Confusion at 16 slowly turns into compromise at 25. Many people end up in careers they didn’t consciously choose, just because they followed a path that was laid out for them without enough exposure or guidance. In my view, the problem is not with students it’s with the ecosystem around them. There is limited access to structured career guidance, minimal industry exposure, and very little focus on helping students understand the practical side of different professions. ▶️ What exists instead is a system that prioritizes marks over direction. Imagine a different approach. If students were introduced early to real-world careers, had access to mentors from different industries, and were encouraged to explore skills beyond textbooks, decision-making would feel less like pressure and more like an informed choice. This is not just an education challenge; it is a workforce challenge for the future. Because the clarity we fail to build at an early stage directly impacts productivity, satisfaction, and innovation later in life. Sai Pavan 1y Report this post In today’s fast-evolving world, career growth is no longer limited to traditional jobs or startup culture alone — it’s about finding where your skills, passion, and purpose meet opportunity. 💼 Jobs give you structure, mentorship, and stability — a platform to learn from experienced leaders and understand how large-scale systems work. 🚀 Startups, on the other hand, give you freedom, creativity, and ownership — a chance to innovate, take risks, and grow beyond limits. Both paths are valuable. What matters most is how you prepare and position yourself to make the most of whichever journey you choose. ✅ How to Secure and Thrive in These Roles: Build strong fundamentals — master your core technical and communication skills. Stay curious — learn beyond your field; explore new technologies and problem-solving methods. Network actively — connect with mentors, peers, and communities that inspire growth. Showcase your work — projects, open-source contributions, or startup ideas show your initiative. Embrace adaptability — whether it’s a corporate role or a startup hustle, flexibility is your greatest asset. At the end of the day, careers aren’t built by titles — they’re built by impact. Ashwina Mathur 7mo Report this post From 0 to 10 LPA — IT Career Roadmap Nobody Tells You Everyone talks about “learn coding and get a job But no one tells you what actually works in 2026. Let me break it down — no fluff, only reality Stage 1: Clarity (Week 1–2) → Stop trying to learn everything → Pick ONE path → Web Development (Frontend / Backend) → Data Analytics (SQL + Power BI / Python) → Python Automation / Backend → Biggest mistake: Jumping between tech stacks Stage 2: Skill Building (Month 1–3) → Don’t just watch tutorials. Build → Learn basics (HTML/CSS/JS OR Python/SQL) → Build 2–3 small projects → Focus on understanding, not memorizing → Example Instead of watching 50 videos Build a simple dashboard / website / automation script Stage 3: Proof of Work (Month 3–5) → This is where 90% people fail → Build 3 strong projects → Solve real-world problems → Upload on GitHub → Post your work on LinkedIn → Example projects → Sales Dashboard (Power BI) → E-commerce Website → Resume Parser (Python) Stage 4: Positioning (Month 5–6) → Skills alone won’t get you hired → Create a strong ATS-friendly resume → Optimize LinkedIn profile (headline + about + projects) → Start posting content (learning + projects) → Recruiters check your presence before your skills Stage 5: Interview Preparation (Month 6–7) → Prepare smartly → Top interview questions (your domain) → Practice explaining your projects clearly → Learn basic problem-solving → If you can’t explain your project, you won’t get selected Stage 6: Apply Smart (Month 7–9) → Don’t apply randomly → Apply daily (10–20 jobs) → Use referrals → Connect with recruiters on LinkedIn → Customize resume for each role Reality Check → If you follow this roadmap consistently → 6–9 months is enough to reach 4–10 LPA → Only if you → Stay consistent → Build projects → Focus on ONE path Most people fail not because IT is hard But because they follow the wrong strategy If you’re serious about breaking into IT in 2026 Comment ROADMAP Let’s grow together 1 Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X To view or add a comment, sign in
